basis_tag: GT-oracle labels on the frozen node set; distances in um
quantity: CANDIDATE-SURFACE REACH of the GATE QUANTITY. Not a score. A rise here is NOT success.

findings.F1_unscaled_flow_is_the_right_gate_quant: reach<=6um rises 0.8969 -> 0.9246 corpus-wide and 0.4753 -> 0.6407 on the bilateral core. The plain kNN16 residual beats raw distance in EVERY state.
findings.F2_the_(L+1)_scaling_is_FALSIFIED_as_a_g: on post_frozen_gap, reach<=6um is raw 0.7280, unscaled residual 0.8325, (L+1)-scaled 0.7353; at 10um the scaled quantity is WORSE than raw (0.9470 vs 0.9717). Mechanism: the flow is rebuilt from the RAW geff edges of that same frame pair, which already span the enlarged interval, so the (L+1) multiplier double-counts the dilation. Lane 2 measured the opposite direction (0.8776 -> 0.9005) using a flow derived from the POST-WRAPPER E0c graph, whose continuations across a frozen interval have already been suppressed - that estimator under-reads the displacement and therefore benefits from scaling. Only the raw-edge flow is available at the point the gate runs, so the scaled variant must not be deployed.
findings.F3_phase_correlation_as_a_VECTOR_is_cata: on the bilateral core, reach<=10um collapses from raw 0.9185 to 0.5691 when the gate is centred on flow + phase-correlation shift; reach<=6um falls 0.4753 -> 0.3728. This independently reconfirms Lane 2 own verdict (valid FLAG, useless VECTOR; 19.2um residual against zero-motion 8.83um) and falsifies surface (iv) as specified.
findings.F4_where_the_mass_is: the largest per-pair gain is on the bilateral core (+16.5 pp at 6um) but that state holds only 810 of 113,875 GT-true pairs (0.71%). ordinary_motion holds 99,795 (87.6%) and also improves (median raw 2.298 -> resid 1.817). The deployable value measured here is a GATE-QUANTITY FIX, not an acquisition-state policy: state routing confines the same fix to a few percent of the mass.
